Executive Order 337-A (1905)

by President of the United States
Placing Administration of Navigation Aids for Tutuila and Other Samoan Islands Under Control of the Department of Commerce and Labor

Executive Order 337-B

→

sister projects: Wikidata item

Signed by President Theodore Roosevelt Monday, July 3, 1905

616150Executive Order 337-A — Placing Administration of Navigation Aids for Tutuila and Other Samoan Islands Under Control of the Department of Commerce and Labor1905President of the United States

It is hereby directed that the Department of Commerce and Labor take charge of and use the proper measures for establishing and maintaining lights and other aids to navigation in the waters of the island of Tutuila and other islands of the Samoan Islands east of longitude 171° west, and have estimates prepared by the Light-House Establishment and submitted to Congress for an appropriation to defray the expenses of the establishment and maintenance of these aids to navigation.

Theodore Roosevelt.

White House,

July 3, 1905.

Signed by President Theodore Roosevelt Monday, July 3, 1905

1905 CSR 89

616073Executive Order 337 — Authorizing Appointment of Charles W. Bell as Finance Clerk in Post-Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules1905President of the United States

The appointment of Charles W. Bell as finance clerk in the post-office at Lowell, Mass., is approved, in view of the fact that authority had been given by the Post-Office Department for the appointment of a finance clerk at that office prior to the transfer of the position to the competitive class.

Theodore Roosevelt.

White House,

July 3, 1905.
